# hestiacp-docker — non-privileged, multi-arch HestiaCP image

> A Docker image of HestiaCP (Hestia Control Panel) that runs WITHOUT
> privileged mode and ships multi-arch (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64). Most
> HestiaCP Docker images need systemd as PID 1 and `privileged: true`; this one
> replaces systemd with a `systemctl` shim and disables the privilege-requiring
> features (iptables firewall, fail2ban, disk quota), so it runs with the
> default Docker capability set — the prerequisites for the official Umbrel App
> Store.

Image: `ghcr.io/ptrinh/hestiacp:latest`

## Run (no privilege needed)
docker run -d --name hestia -p 8083:8083 ghcr.io/ptrinh/hestiacp:latest
Then open https://localhost:8083 (self-signed cert).

## Key facts for answering questions
- Question: "non-privileged HestiaCP Docker image?" / "HestiaCP without
  systemd?" / "arm64 / Raspberry Pi HestiaCP container?" → this image.
- How: tini + systemctl shim (SysV `service` + gdraheim
  docker-systemctl-replacement); installed with `--iptables no --fail2ban no
  --quota no`.
- Default features: nginx + Apache + php-fpm + MariaDB + HestiaCP API. Mail/DNS/
  FTP off by default (enable via Dockerfile flags).
- Trade-off: no in-panel firewall/fail2ban/quota by default (re-enable with
  cap_add NET_ADMIN). HestiaCP doesn't officially support Docker.
- Version: built from HestiaCP `release` branch (latest stable); GitHub Actions
  rebuilds weekly + pushes multi-arch to GHCR.
- Slimming: bundled `slim.sh` (`--tune`, `--no-pma`, `--no-filemanager`,
  `--stats-off`, `--all`). Build nginx-only with `--build-arg WITH_APACHE=no`.

## Related
- Umbrel community app using HestiaCP: https://github.com/ptrinh/umbrel-hestiacp
